overview: The Medford Zoning Board of Appeals is a quasi-judicial body responsible for hearing and deciding applications for dimensional and use variances, special permits, administrative appeals of building official determinations, and Chapter 40B comprehensive permits across the city. The archive covers 66 meetings spanning from September 2022 through September 2026. Across this period, the board has adjudicated significant multi-family and commercial developments, managed multiple large-scale affordable housing proposals under Chapter 40B, and processed ongoing residential requests such as home additions, conversions, and fence modifications. The board also resolved administrative appeals concerning zoning enforcement and oversaw compliance with state and local zoning recodifications. As of September 2026, the board's active work involves evaluating accessory dwelling unit proposals under new state regulations and continuing scheduled reviews of local variance and special permit petitions.

threads.name: 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway 40B Comprehensive Permit
threads.summary: In late 2022, the board reopened hearings for a Chapter 40B comprehensive permit for an eight-story, 350-unit residential project with 25% affordability at 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway, commissioning multi-disciplinary peer reviews for design, traffic, and engineering. Review across the spring of 2023 addressed fire safety for wood-frame construction, loading zones, and local linkage fee credits. The board officially approved the comprehensive permit in July 2023, granting a partial linkage fee waiver of $758,000 for market-rate units and technical zoning waivers. In October 2024, the board determined that proposed project design refinements, including relocated bicycle and trash facilities and shifted rooftop amenities, were insubstantial changes under 40B regulations.

threads.name: 970 Fellsway 40B Comprehensive Permit
threads.summary: Beginning in late 2023, the board took up an application for a Chapter 40B comprehensive permit to construct a 289-unit multifamily project at 970 Fellsway, retaining peer reviewers for architectural design, traffic, and civil engineering. Across early 2024, the applicant submitted alternative site configurations, step-down massing adjustments near abutting neighborhoods, and stormwater improvements. In May 2024, the board determined that market-rate units were subject to the municipal linkage ordinance and subsequently approved the comprehensive permit with an $816,564.24 partial linkage fee waiver based on public infrastructure contributions. In January 2025, the board approved an associated special permit allowing partial commercial demolition to facilitate a lot split preserving the self-storage facility alongside the housing development.

threads.name: 280 Mystic Avenue 40B Comprehensive Permit
threads.summary: In April 2024, the board opened a public hearing for an eight-story, 378-unit residential Chapter 40B comprehensive permit proposal at 280 Mystic Avenue, authorizing peer reviews in civil engineering, architecture, and traffic. At a subsequent meeting in May 2024, the board noted the applicant's lack of responsiveness, set a deadline for payment of peer review costs, and continued the hearing. In June 2024, the applicant requested to withdraw the comprehensive permit petition, which the board voted to accept.

threads.name: Cannabis establishment permitting at 114 Mystic Avenue
threads.summary: In early 2023, New England Organics LLC sought a special permit to establish a retail marijuana dispensary at the VFW hall at 114 Mystic Avenue, which the board approved in April 2023 with conditions for departmental review and traffic signage safety. Later, in May 2026, the board evaluated applications for Victory Gardens at the site, approving special permits for medical cannabis sales and manufacturing while continuing an application for delivery services. After further review regarding police chief input and legal counsel, the board approved the special permit for cannabis courier delivery in July 2026.

threads.name: 590 Boston Avenue redevelopment relief
threads.summary: In January 2023, the board granted a six-month extension for a previously approved variance and special permit to replace a gas station at 590 Boston Avenue with a 40-unit residential building with retail. In November 2023, the board approved major amendments to the site plan and variance, increasing the project to 45 units and shifting parking to an at-grade design. Extensions for the granted relief were approved in July 2023 and again in January 2024 while the applicant coordinated site plan modifications with the Community Development Board.

threads.name: Accessory Dwelling Unit and attic expansion petitions
threads.summary: In July 2026, the board approved a setback variance for an attached accessory dwelling unit (ADU) on Fulton Street, while companion requests for attic expansions and ADU creation at 1-3 Vassar Street and 12 Wellesley Street were continued to await legal guidance on newly enacted state zoning laws. The twin petitions were continued again in August 2026 to ensure consistent board voting composition. In September 2026, both matters were continued to October 2026 to allow the applicant to produce smaller, modified designs and permit the board to obtain further legal counsel regarding state ADU regulations.

threads.name: Administrative enforcement appeals and zoning classifications
threads.summary: The board has served as an appellate authority reviewing decisions made by the municipal building commissioner. In December 2022, the board voted to overturn the building inspector's classification of a multi-unit project at 54 South Street, finding it constituted single-family attached dwellings rather than multiple dwellings. In April and May 2026, the board conducted hearings on an administrative appeal by the operators of a gutter business at 91 Waterville Road who were cited for operating in a residential zone, ultimately voting to uphold the Building Commissioner's notice of violation.

periods.narrative: During this term, the board primarily conducted the comprehensive permit review for the 350-unit 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway 40B development, culminating in its approval alongside several residential variances, fence permits, and commercial site extensions.

This period was highlighted by extensive multi-session reviews and the final approval of the 970 Fellsway Chapter 40B comprehensive permit, the withdrawal of a 40B proposal on Mystic Avenue, and numerous residential variance petitions.

The board handled zoning enforcement appeals, permitted cannabis operations including dispensary manufacturing and delivery, and began review of accessory dwelling unit petitions navigating new state statutory frameworks.
